newsitem.title: HONG KONG: TENNIS-MUSTER THREATENS TO QUIT DAVIS CUP.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MUSTER THREATENS TO QUIT DAVIS CUP.

text.p: Austria's Thomas Muster, still incensed at abuse directed at him in a Davis Cup tie in Brazil last month, said on Tuesday he would rather stop playing in the competition than risk injury at the hands of unruly fans.
World number three Muster marched off court during the clash between Austria and Brazil in Sao Paulo, saying he felt threatened by the crowd.
The International Tennis Federation (ITF) last week ordered Austria to forfeit $59,000 prize money for failing to complete the tie and upheld $8,000 fines imposed on the spot against Muster.
Muster, in Hong Kong for an exhibition event with world number one Pete Sampras and French Open champion Yevgeny Kafelnikov, defended his actions and said the referee's report was nonsense.
"If the ITF continues to support these countries and they continue to cause trouble, sooner or later somebody is going to be injured," he said.
"But it will not be me. I am not interested in playing Davis Cup again (in those circumstances). It is not sport. I will play next year and see (what happens).
"Of course the ITF is going to believe its own referee -- I have read the report and it is nonsense. I know when it is getting dangerous (on court).
"It is easy for somebody at home watching on television to make a comment but it was me out there.
"They have fined me for leaving the court -- I have no choice but to pay the fine."
